ticket.created: Emit After the Write

createTicket still does exactly one job of its own — insert the row — and adds a single emit() once that's actually committed.

// Figure 5.2: creating a ticket now announces it too (src/services/ticket.service.js, excerpt)
export const createTicket = async ({ subject, description, customerId }) => {
  const ticket = await prisma.ticket.create({
    data: { subject, description, customerId },
    include: {
      customer: userSummary,
    },
  });

  domainEvents.emit(EVENTS.TICKET_CREATED, ticket);

  return ticket;
};

Two details here matter more than they look. First, emit() runs after await prisma.ticket.create(...) has already resolved — the row genuinely exists in the database before anything is told about it. Emitting first and inserting second would risk a listener reacting to a ticket that then fails to actually get created (a Prisma error, a validation edge case) — announcing something that never really happened. Second, the payload is the same ticket object createTicket already has on hand, customer include and all, not just an id. Every listener in this lesson needs the customer's email or name for an email/notification message; passing the full object once here means no listener has to re-query Prisma for data the service already fetched.

domainEvents.emit() itself doesn't return anything meaningful and doesn't block on what listeners do with it — createTicket calls it, moves on to return ticket, and has no idea whether zero listeners or three reacted, or what any of them did. That's deliberate: the previous topic's whole point was that this function's job ends at "announce it happened."
